newsitem.title: UK: Smith & Nephew dips as profits fall short.
newsitem.headline: Smith & Nephew dips as profits fall short.

text.p: Shares in Smith & Nephew Plc fell slightly in pre-market trading on Tuesday after the healthcare products group posted a one percent rise in full-year pre-tax profits to 182.4 million stg, at the low end of expectations.

The stock was down 2p at 189 by 0810 GMT. Analyst profit expectations had mostly been in a range between 182.0 million stg and 185 million. Smith & Nephew's dividend of 6p was also no better than expected.

"We are not surprised to see the shares opening a bit lower," said Alyson Coates, analyst at SocGen, pointing out that the strong pound and launch costs of S&N's new Dermagraft bio-engineered skin tissue replacement product would restrict profit growth in the current year.

"The company is developing its exposure in developing markets but it is still working hard to deliver underlying growth in the mid single digit range," Coates said, adding that benefits from Dermagraf would likely not fully emerge until 1998.
However she said the company was well placed to make an acquisition, with gearing of just 15 percent.

Peter Cartwright, analyst at Williams de Broe, said there was no immediate reason from the results to change his "hold" stance on the stock, pointing out that the statement was in line with S&N's trading statement in January.
"The picture looks as if it will improve in 1998," Cartwright said, "but that is sufficiently far enough away for there to be no hurry to get involved."

Smith & Nephew said its underlying sales rose six percent in a year when market conditions were "if anything, tougher than 1995," with selling price reductions which were particularly severe in North America.
The company said conditions in its main markets were likely to remain tough for some time, though "these markets remain intrinsically sound with above-average long-term growth prospects."

Market share has been steadily increased -- as well as involvement in new technologies being developed -- giving the group "the potential to generate substantial and sustained sales and profits growth into the next century."
